aspect: The rule that created the practice
description: No conjugal visits are granted to Palestinian security prisoners. For a wife whose husband is serving decades, that is a decision about her fertility made by a prison service.
energy_note: Your reproductive life, administered by a jail.

description: Ammar Ziben, serving 32 life sentences, smuggled a sample to his wife. Their son Mohannad was born by caesarean on 13 August 2012 at the Razan fertility clinic in Nablus, and the case opened the way for dozens of other prisoners' wives.
energy_note: Thirty-two life sentences, and a son.

description: Razan in Nablus received one or two smuggled samples a week in 2013, kept about 65 frozen at -196C and had put 22 women through IVF. Counts of babies born vary by date: 32 over three years, about 50 by early 2018, over 60 by late 2018, some 120 in a little over a decade. ICSI is used because the samples arrive degraded.
energy_note: Sixty-plus children, conceived through a prison wall.
notes: The clinic's director refused funding from both Hamas and Fatah, saying the interest was humanitarian rather than political.

aspect: The state's response was to deny the children papers
description: Israel has denied identification documents or legal status to babies born this way, and those children are denied visits to their imprisoned fathers. Surveillance cameras were installed in cells and visitation was tightened after births peaked in 2015.
energy_note: A child with no papers, barred from meeting his father.

aspect: The woman carries the reputational risk
description: Families and friends are deliberately involved in the process so that the wife's reputation is protected and the community accepts the child is the result of science rather than sin. The protection has to be organised in advance because the suspicion is assumed.
energy_note: Arranging witnesses to your own pregnancy.

aspect: It is simultaneously a private decision and a public statement
description: The births are reported, dedicated, and read politically by everyone. A woman's decision to have a child becomes a national event she did not necessarily want to host.
